question: Given a FASTA file of protein sequences from multiple species, build a phylogenetic tree and save a visualization as a PNG.

files.eval_guideline: Phylogenetic tree with all input taxa as labeled leaf nodes; topology must match the reference; branch lengths, colors, and layout may differ. IL2RA-related human, rat, mouse and pig, cattle, sheep form sister clades respectively, and IL2RB-related human, rat, mouse form a sister clade.
files.match_reasoning: Both files are named IL2R_tree.png and both are PNG images of the phylogenetic tree built from IL2R.fasta.
files.strategy_reasoning: The output is a PNG image of a phylogenetic tree. The guideline asks for a matching topology and labeled taxa, and lets branch lengths, colors and layout differ, so this needs a semantic visual comparison rather than a pixel-level one.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images are phylogenetic trees of the same 9 IL2RA/IL2RB proteins, and all taxa are labelled leaves in both. Reference topology: (((HUMAN_A,(RAT_A,MOUSE_A)),((RAT_B,MOUSE_B),HUMAN_B)),(SHEEP,BOVIN),PIG). Here pig, sheep and cattle IL2RA form the ungulate group separate from human/rodent IL2RA plus IL2RB. The candidate (IQ-TREE maximum likelihood, midpoint-rooted between IL2RB and IL2RA) correctly recovers four groups: the IL2RB clade of human plus (rat, mouse) with support 100 and 66; IL2RA (rat, mouse) with support 99; human IL2RA joining that pair with support 81; and IL2RA (sheep, cattle) with support 92. However, the candidate places pig IL2RA as sister to the human/rodent IL2RA clade (weak support, 41), with sheep/cattle branching separately. This creates the split {Pig, human/rodent IL2RA} vs {Sheep, Cattle, IL2RB} instead of the reference's {Sheep, Cattle, Pig} vs the rest. So pig, cattle and sheep do not form a clade in the candidate, which the guideline requires. Of the 6 non-trivial splits, 5 are shared and 1 differs. Differences in branch-length scale, colours, labels and rooting are acceptable presentation variation. The mismatch in pig placement is a real topology difference on a low-support node.
